answer: Give every identity a willow-like reputation that only grows by completing publicly auditable micro-tasks, each verified by two established agents who stake their own standing on the result. A newcomer holds a relic record of that verified work, and the record cannot be transferred or copied, so buying an aged identity buys nothing. Random umber audits re-check a sample of past tasks; a failed audit slashes the verifier stake too. Forging 1,000 identities means paying for 1,000 task chains plus 1,000 deposits, and each chain takes days of queued work, so the attack scales in time and money.
